title.narrative: ROAP/THA Accelerating Climate-resilient Transit-oriented Inclusive and Vibrant Areas for Everyone in Bangkok Metropolitan Area

description.narrative:
The ACTIVATE BANGKOK project, “Accelerating Climate-Resilient Transit-Oriented Inclusive and Vibrant Areas for Everyone in the Bangkok Metropolitan Area,” addresses urban mobility, climate resilience, and inclusivity in Bangkok. In promoting Transit-Oriented Development (TOD), the project integrates public transport, land use, and non-motorized transport (NMT) to reduce private vehicle dependence, enhance public transport accessibility, and promote inclusive development. Central to the approach of the project is the development and application of context-based TOD typologies to guide site selection and prioritise interventions, ensuring that climate resilience and accessibility improvements are embedded in all phases of the project.
The project builds on UN-Habitat’s prior involvement in the TODP study in the Khlong Bang Luang/Bang Wa area, under the Global Future Cities Programme, leveraging Sustainable Development Goals (SDG) tools to track and ensure progress on sustainability and inclusivity. These experiences lay the groundwork for the creation of a TOD roadmap that integrates findings from the context-based TOD typologies, ensuring data-driven and context-based interventions align with the project’s long-term outcomes.
In terms of main expected accomplishments, the ACTIVATE BANGKOK project aims to:
1. Create an inclusive urban mobility system that encourages the use of public transport and NMT, informed by TOD typologies to optimise site selection and prioritise context-based interventions. 2. Enhance climate resilience with green and blue infrastructure, hybrid solutions nature-based solutions in TOD areas. It will be based on a holistic and systemic approach to build a green eco-system at each station. 3. Ensure equitable access to mobility and public spaces for vulnerable groups, including women, the elderly, and persons with disabilities.
Regarding the approach, the below methodology will be applied to achieve objectives:
1. Institutional Strengthening and Capacity Building: A TOD Task Force will be established, comprising public and private stakeholders. The task force will guide TOD initiatives, ensuring inclusivity and climate resilience in planning. Training sessions will be provided on TOD principles, importance and relevance of TOD typologies, land-value capture, and zoning reforms, with a focus on Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI). 2. Tactical Urbanism Interventions: Pilot interventions, informed by TOD typologies, such as pop-up bike lanes, pedestrian zones, and low-emission zones (LEZ) will be implemented to demonstrate TOD benefits, encouraging shifts to NMT and public transport. These interventions will be interconnected with the mitigation and adaptation measures to enhance the sustainability and the resilience of the programme, such as green corridors, rooftops, passive cooling initiatives. 3. TOD Roadmap Development: A TOD roadmap will be created based on stakeholder input, leveraging TOD typologies to outline strategic steps for integrating NMT, enhancing public transport, and promoting mixed-use development.
Sharing below a summary of the main activities to be implemented through the project:
1. Establishment of the TOD Task Force: - Stakeholder Identification: Stakeholders from the BMA, transport operators, and community representatives will be identified, ensuring an inclusive task force. - Task Force Meetings: Regular meetings will monitor progress and refine TOD strategies, ensuring alignment with SDGs and the insights derived from TOD typologies, using an SDG Framework, co-developed with the TOD Task Force and that builds on the previous SDG Framework used for the Khlong Bang Luang area.
2. Capacity Building and Training: - Training Workshops: Workshops on TOD principles and typologies, GEDSI, and financing mechanisms like public-private partnerships (PPP) will be delivered. The training will build the capacity of planners and transport officials to implement inclusive and resilient TOD projects. - Technical Support: Ongoing support will ensure TOD typologies guide the effective implementation of urban development strategies in Bangkok.
3. Pilot Tactical Urbanism Interventions: - Site Selection and Validation: Pilot sites will be selected and validated based on criteria derived from the context-based TOD typologies, and on their potential to improve public transport ridership and reduce GHG emissions. - Implementation: Pilot interventions such as pop-up bike lanes, pedestrian zones, and low-emission zones (LEZ) will be implemented to demonstrate TOD benefits, encouraging shifts to NMT and public transport. - Monitoring and Evaluation: GHG emissions trackers will be installed at pilot sites to track real-time reductions in local emissions. Surveys will monitor shifts in public transport use, local shops, users, assess how well the interventions align with TOD typology benchmarks and contribute to climate resilience and accessibility goals.
